I've played this game about 300-400hrs [outdated 400hrs +] (playing since August 2015) and since steam release I nearly stopped playing it at all. I'll mention the "why" in my review. (The two reasons mentioned below are since steam release, never really had these situations before)
The game itself is great, especially for those of you who played PR.
Atm it's just infantry based combat in Desert or Forest environments, but highly tactical and works best with COMMUNICATION!
And there is the first reason why I don't recommend this game.
There are WAY to many people playing this game who don't communicate with each other, maybe in the squad itself but most squad LEADERS don't talk to each other, which results in total chaos. Every squad does their own thing and are scattered all over the map.
To find a server where this is not the case you'll search for hours... if you're on a server where the communication works appropriately you'll get the best combat experience you ever had in a game!
Another feature that's available atm and that'll be expanded over the time is the abillity to set up FOBs (Forward operating Bases) which you can expand with barricades and hopefully cal. 50s or similar in later patches.
And there is the second reason that is completely destroying my experience in this game.
There are WAY to many people who're thinking that it's a good idea to play minecraft the whole match and build a massive super FOB (mostly ones which are placed on flags). Not that it's bad to build fobs, but you should make sure that you're capable of defending it.
In most games you got 3 of about 5 squads camping at one flag and barricading themselfes... so you got a compound filled with about 20-30 people... those of you who got an idea which impact explosives like 30mm grenades or frag grenades got in a closed off Compound filled with ~25 people know why this is a bad idea.
As I said before... if you don't have this scenario and 1-2 squads are actually defending the d-flag without doing the above mentioned and if the communications work appropriately ...
... YOU WILL HAVE THE BEST TIME OF YOU LIFE!
YOU'LL HAVE:
- Intense combat situations which mostly consists of you sitting behind cover, crying and sh***ing your brand new camo pants!
- Tactical approach towards enemy flags or bases!
- 15-50 people working together to show the enemy that they stand no chance!
- Beautiful detailed maps based on real satelite data!
- The best sounddesign in a shooter I've ever heard
- No weapon customisation with cute little stickers and doodads... NO, this is WAR! Go HARD or go HOME!
I really really like this game and can recommend it to everyone! BUT play the game how it's meant to be played!
Talk to other people and only play squadleader if you'll make arrangements with the other squads!
Think twice if whatever you're doing is useful, for example building a fob on a d-flag... No! It's probably not because if you can't hold your flag you'll lose the FOB too... this means you'll lose at least 20 tickets for nothing! Think about if it's better to place an FOB and don't expand it so that enemy forces have to search it rather than display it on the top of the hill... Your decissions as squad leader are GAMECHANGING so think them through!

A brilliant puzzle game couched in a unique and engaging scifi story/philosophical meditation - there's really nothing else like it. The puzzles themselves are excellent - thoughtful and well designed with a wide variety of mechanics which are gradually introduced over the course of the game. The pacing is spot-on, with puzzles designed to produce that "aha!" moment when you work out a new way to use the tools you've been given, and more complex puzzles designed to force you to integrate all that knowledge into a larger cohesive solution. There is no shortage of puzzle here, either, the game remains interesting and continues to require real thought all the way through its ~100 puzzles. It also offers a host of diabolically clever optional things to find and puzzle out - all told it will keep you busy for quite some time if you're a completionist. On the strength of the core gameplay alone, I'd recommend it.
But then there's everything else: the beautiful score, the lovely environments, the evocative atmosphere, and the fantastic writing. The story is told through fragments in text and audio, as well as interactions with a very few characters. The voice acting is all top-notch, and the entire story is exceedingly well done.
There are very few missteps here, the only thing I would cite is the very last puzzle (for the "best" ending) is a bit too "boss battle" for my tastes and would benefit from some intermediate checkpointing. Still, it's a minor scuff on a masterpiece of a game.
I would enthusiastically recommend the game and, further, would strongly suggest you go in as blind as possible. It's an outstanding game and an outstanding experience, no outside sources needed.

Like Prison Architect (in art style) meets Dwarf Fortress, but without as much complexity or depth (literal and figurative).
Whereas in Dwarf Fortress the UI is a mess and you can dig through many layers and do many many things, Rimworld seemingly decided to start with the bare-bones of making a user-friendly UI and build up from there.
The game is in Alpha 14 at the time of writing this but it feels pretty complete in the early-game. There is plenty to do and build for long enough to keep you coming back for days, but as you advance your colony you may realize the game slows down a bit as it goes on. This is likely just a product of Alpha-ness that will be addressed in future updates though, I can't imagine the developer doesn't have lots of plans.
That said, when you start installing Mods and Mod-packs is when this game *really* shines. Between the "Hardcore SK" mod pack, "Mega MOD Pack", or many others, the game turns from a bare-bones almost-Dwarf Fortress into a game truly capable of standing up in its' own right.
The mod community for this game is huge and adds a lot to this type of game; From combat "realism" overhauls, to new structures/production/technology trees, to even new character traits, mods turn this game up to 11.

First the positives...
I remember Doom in the 90s, the corridors of pipes and panels on the walls and ceilings... but it was a flat repetitive  tiled  texture. Fast forward to today and those pipes, panels, wiring and countless other sci-fi furnishings clutter the area in glorious detailed 3D, with no noticeable tiling. This is significant. It's a long way from Doom corridors. The tiling is still there, but it's hard to spot. Great stuff.
Nice soundtrack. Normally I turn music off completely in games but this was subtle and mostly complemented the action.
Some negatives...
The detail gets a bit fuzzy when you're too close to an object, but that's not a big deal. What's worse is the distant buildings. They seem out of focus, and I'm wondering whether DOF is mandatory, which is a shame if so. I hate depth of field, it makes no sense to have this lens effect. I want my eye's aperture to be deep, thanks. When I look at things in sunlight in the day, I don't see blurry DOF focus. Get rid of  DOF, it's fake and I really don't like DOF.
The game holds your hand too much, to the point of blatant arrows pointing where to go.
I got the feeling it dials back the difficulty if you're stuck on a section. I really don't like that. Sometimes it just takes a few goes to get through. I don't want the game making adjustments because it thinks I want it to be easier.
I wish the world was more open, there's not really any chance of getting lost. Sometimes it seems you could jump over a fence, but the game doesn't want you to because there's only one way to go, and that's not over the fence.
I suppose in GTA we can't just go into any building and get incredible details like on the outside, but it would be nice if someone could make a truly open world both exterior and interior with huge variety.
I'm keen to see where this game engine  goes. I like the rich, solid look it brings. But it seems to compromise on other things to achieve that richness. It's worth keeping an eye on, and I will check out other games that use it.

The kind of game only the geniuses at Rockstar could muster up. The cutscenes feel like your watching a pulp action film, the gameplay, for what is the most part a cover shooter is tough, and brings back memories of my favorite scenes in John Woo's Hard Boiled. The Bullet Camera never get's old, and I love having the ability to slow it down even more. Enemies react realistically to gunshots, the point of entry/exit is incredibly detailed and realistic as well. I bought the collectors edition for this when it first came out on the 360 and have played through the story about 3 or 4 times, 33% of the way through my second playthrough on PC. It will never get old. Except for the Stadium. God I hate that level.
The game ran fairly well on my old 2 GB EVGA GTX 650 TI BOOST, but it really shines on my MSI GTX 770 TwinFrozr, constant 60 FPS on Ultra. I do, however, keep a few unnecessary settings turned down. The graphical options for the game are great, varied and well explained. There's a description for every option and a bar that tells you exactly how much VRAM the game is using, which really needs to be in more games.
The multiplayer however, even when it was still very active, felt incredibly subpar. The main reason I only played the online component on my 360 was to prepare my friends and I for GTA V, as the crews ( essentially clans that leveled up while offering absolutely no perks/pros in MP3 for doing so, AFAIK) were usable in both games. The last time I checked, (yesterday at the time of this writing) the Online for the game was completely dead. Attempting to join a match on PC threw me into a lobby by myself. My online character also lost their face at one point while I was perusing the rather shoddy character customization, and for just a second there I thought I was playing AC: Unity.
If for some reason after all the steam sales you've thrown your wallet at you still don't have it, and you want to play a mature, gritty and unique Rockstar game and don't quite have the dosh for GTA V (or played the life out of it on a console) wait for it to go on sale and don't bother buying any DLC, as the online is dead. You can get it for a few bucks, and the game is long for a no frills 3rd person shooter.
Pros:
+Game still looks amazing, and it's turning 3 this year!
+Solid gameplay, you will feel like a bad♥♥♥♥♥playing this 11 times out of 10.
+Mature story, blew me away the first time I played it and still amazes me today.
+You can get it for really cheap during a sale, just don't buy the season pass/any DLC. It's all for the dead online.
+Max's sarcastic narration and self pitying attitude really flesh him out as a character, as opposed to serious military guy that we see all too often nowadays.
+ The voice acting in this is top-notch.
+Max doesn't speak Portugese and he's in Brazil. There are no magic english subtitles to help you, so unless you speak Portugese, you're SOL. This helps immerse the player by making them feel just as lost and confused to the whole situation as Max is.
Cons:
-Subpar multiplayer is dead.
-Rockstar Social Club.
-One level that I personally did not enjoy, which was the one in the soccer stadium.
Overall: 8.9 painkillers out of 10.

It's been almost two months since I finished this game and I still find myself thinking about it.
The puzzle elements have a way of surprising you with how they can be used. I recall one puzzle with a hexahedron and a mine that was borderline deceptive, but for the most part the puzzles were fair and incredibly satisfying. The ancient ruins theme coupled with futuristic technology made for an interesting world to walk around in.
I'm also fascinated by the philosophy of AI and the implications AI has for how we think about the nature of consciousness and self-awareness. The computer terminals and the audio time capsules built upon these ideas while tying into the story within the game. The library assistant which you debate with through the terminals also had that balanced mix of intelligent thought and entertaining character.
This game was a double-whammy of excellent puzzle mechanics and thought-provoking concepts (that will definitely become more relevant with age). If you're into both those things, you're in for a treat. It's one of those games I wish I could forget so I could play it all over again, but I doubt I'll be forgetting it anytime soon!

I was very sceptical whether or not to buy this game to begin with.  However, now I have played it for over 40 hours, I can see why reviews don't really say much about the game.  The more appealling features of this game are the repeated "eureka" moments throughout, and the less you know the better.  Exploring, finding things out, discovering "outside-of-the-box" ways of doing something, or stumbling upon the less-obvious, is what makes this game special.
Gameplay itself is straightforward and there's a multitude of options to tweak, and a decent selection of settings for motion-sickness sufferers.  I never played 3rd person once, so cannot comment on that.
Graphics and visuals are nice.  3D geometry can be quite basic on some objects and in some areas, although this has been well disguised by high resolution textures and not that noticeable.  The ice crystals of snow, grains of sand, and the texture of stone, for example, are well defined and very clear.  There are a decent selection of settings to adjust, and although I have never tried lower settings when playing on my decent PC; my VERY low-spec Linux system ran the game at about 10fps (AMD Athlon II x2 250 : GeForce 210) so it should run on lower spec PCs with sacrifices.
All in all, I am impressed with The Talos Principle.  It's taken a few simple ideas and added so much depth that it's no longer skin-deep.  Polished, refined and detailed spring to mind; which is far more important to me than incredibly complex and shallow.

If you're looking for a senseless shoot-em-up that delivers, Wolfenstein is the way to go.
Wolfenstein: The New Order takes place after the 2009 Wolfenstein game, which takes place after another Wolfenstein game, which takes place after another Wolfenstein game. Yes I know, its not that confusing now isn't it?
The Nazis have taken over the world. Yay to Hitler and all that nonsense. Your job, is to do something which I like to call "Endless slaughter" of Nazis. That's essentially the whole game, walk about, see Nazis, kill them all.
However, there is a story to the game and as it progresses, you'll feel a sense of sadness as SPOILER ALERT, people die. Okay, not that big of a spoiler. But still. The ending of the game was brilliant, you'll feel a sense of accomplishment as well as sadness at the same time. Seriously. Tear jerk moment alert.
Now on to the gameplay.
Combat is fantastic, you move around shooting, weapons have alternative firemodes which I might say, some are pretty neat. Stealth on the other hand, is in my opinion, pretty damn useless unless you're doing it on the higher difficulties. It's boring, you go around knocking around the commanders and its a pretty dull experience compared to the typical "GET SOME", guns blazing thing. Yes, I prefer loud combat. Weapons get crazier as you progress, from normal WW2 rifles to laser rifles from the moon.
Best part? You don't even have to aim down your sights if you want an old school feel-aiming down your sights is as useless as vegetables during a sasuage, I mean, meat fest. It's there, but you hardly use that. I♥♥♥♥♥♥you not, accuracy is overrated in this game especially in the later levels, where your guns have close to unlimited ammo. (The lazer ones anyway).
Sound-wise, the soundtrack is awesome and you'll feel a sense of rock and roll' as you gun your way through hoards of Nazis. Additionally, the German voice acting in this game is superb!
MY ONLY PROBLEM WITH THIS GAME?
The Anti-Ailising on this game is NON EXISTANT. You'll see line tears half the time and that pisses me off, it wasn't till the end of the game till I found out that AA was actually in the game--you just had to throw it in via console. Seriously?
However, this game runs well at max settings on a core i5-3570k and a GTX 970 (I know, its overpowered, but its fine) at 1080p. Won't recommend 4k resolutions though if you use a 970, save that for x2 980Tis or something of a higher league.
Pros
- Endless shooting
- Great voice acting
- Incredible combat
- Great story
- Great soundtrack
Cons
- Not enough Nazis to kill
- Pretty short-mid? It's about 6 Hours long, should be longer for a 40GB game...YES, 40GB.
- 40GB download. What the hell

TL;DR buy Return to Castle Wolfenstein instead. It's cheaper and much better.
Pros:
+Looks amazing, even on low settings
+All guns except the assault rifle feel good
+Good sound design
+Solid controls
+Lengthy
+Second boss fight is good
+Good set pieces
+Pretty good AI, especially for a modern FPS
Netural points:
-You're most effective staying in cover, which contradicts the fast movement speed. Most gunfights I spent hiding in one corner ducking in and going back out when I had more health. This is not an old school shooter just because it has health kits and fast movement.
-Some very confronting imagery, and has a very dark tone overall.
-Recharging the laser guns got annoying, considering they are the most effective guns in the game, but at the same time this probably balances them
-Some story points are very over the top
-No multiplayer
Cons:
-Story wise, it doesn't know if it wants to be dark and gritty or some over the top B-movie style thing. Either one is fine, but together they undermind each other.
-The relationship between BJ and Anya was lazy (basically two cringe-worthy sex scenes and then all the sudden BJ wants to live his life with Anya)
-There are a few sections were they jam enemies with a lot of health and automatic shotguns in tight corridors.
-Although the weapons are fun, there aren't many.
-Overcharging health is a waste of time until the last boss fight
-Having to press 'E' to pick up ammo in a fast paced shooter is annoying. It also got me killed once when I accidently picked up a big machine gun instead of ammo.
-Some fetch quests early on
-Assault rifle shakes around like BJ is having a seizure when ever you fire a burst
-Some later levels have a lot of dust/smoke particals, which although looks good, makes it a pain to see
-Level layout could be better. During the destroyed bridge level, there is a checkpoint on a metal beam, which goes down to a platform. If you go this way, you end up sandwich between an Ubersoldat (big and powerful enemy) and at least 4-5 soldiers and a guy with a rocket launcher. What you're suppose to do is go down into a train which is hanging down, and climb down so all the enemies are in front of you and you can deal with them seperately.

I highly encourage you to buy this game. It is very thought-provoking. It has well-designed puzzles. It has great soundtrack, beautiful locales and amazing atmosphere. And really leaves an emotional impact. If ever we need to build a real EL facility, this game would be among the first things to put into the archives.
This game is a 99% pure puzzle game in terms of it's mechanics: there is no platforming, there are very few timers (other than the ones you set for yourself) and there is pretty much no physics involved in solutions (not counting the pressure plates, that might as well be a switch with keys). Just you, the environment and pure unhindered logic. The developers went out of their way to remove any possible distractions or confusions from the environment.
Solving puzzles in this game is like solving a mathematical equation, only more fun. Some will like it. Some will hate it. I liked it, it was a nice change of pace from portal with it's timers and navigation puzzles or Trine 2 with it's physics puzzles. Ultimately whether you like Talos's mechanics will be up to you and I encourage you to play the demo before buying to see for yourself.
However the other aspect of this game is what really grabbed my attention: it's incredible atmosphere. All of the game's elements - the puzzles, the environments, the philosophical discussions, excerpts from various old myths and philosophical works on the nature of intelligence, life and personality contribute to this great atmosphere.
Talos Priciple presents it's story in an excellent way. Very few works of art do it better, be it a game or otherwise. If you played Half Life 2 or watch the movie Lost, you are familiar with the approach where the plot is given to you in pieces, glimpses of the mystery, with a vital piece that puts it all together being at the end. It keeps you interested in the story, but is very frustrating when the amount of information given seems too small or too dispárate to be connected to what you already know. Talos Principle does away with that problem by pacing out it's story almost perfectly. You always know exactly how the new piece of information relates to what you already know. Yet you never know too much.
I was very motivated, to the end, to find and read all the documents available, to find and listen to all the amazingly voice acted and written audio logs. And that, as far as I am concerned, means the game is worth playing for the story and the atmosphere alone.
Although I never did find the answer to the main mystery of the game, I finished the game completely satisfied and maybe that was the whole point: the end result isn't as important as what you do to get there.

Rimworld is a colony builder sim similar to games like dwarf fortress and dungeon keeper. It looks like prison architect, but dont be fooled by its simple art style, its has a complex combat system takes into account things like visibility, cover, weather and injuries.
The difficulty level in the game is dictated by storyteller ai that throw different events at you. Storytellers range from merciful to sadistic and help create moments of desperation and victory that make this game so intriguing.

The game is easily modded and tweaked, and regularly updated. The dev Tynan Sylvester and his team are really dedicated and post up regular updates on the dev blog.
Some of my experiences with the recent updates include: Having to store human bodies for the winter when a blight wiped out most of my crops. Harvesting a colonist's captured pirate uncle for organs  when said colonist lost a lung fighting said uncle. A love story unfolded between a dull farm boy and a 3000 year old aristocrat, the farm boy ended up sacrificing his life to save the artistocrat when a cougar went mad and attacked the colony during the wedding ceremony. This game is all about the joyful and dark moments you'll experience with your little colony.

I've played this game about 300-400hrs [outdated 400hrs +] (playing since August 2015) and since steam release I nearly stopped playing it at all. I'll mention the "why" in my review. (The two reasons mentioned below are since steam release, never really had these situations before)
The game itself is great, especially for those of you who played PR.
Atm it's just infantry based combat in Desert or Forest environments, but highly tactical and works best with COMMUNICATION!
And there is the first reason why I don't recommend this game.
There are WAY to many people playing this game who don't communicate with each other, maybe in the squad itself but most squad LEADERS don't talk to each other, which results in total chaos. Every squad does their own thing and are scattered all over the map.
To find a server where this is not the case you'll search for hours... if you're on a server where the communication works appropriately you'll get the best combat experience you ever had in a game!
Another feature that's available atm and that'll be expanded over the time is the abillity to set up FOBs (Forward operating Bases) which you can expand with barricades and hopefully cal. 50s or similar in later patches.
And there is the second reason that is completely destroying my experience in this game.
There are WAY to many people who're thinking that it's a good idea to play minecraft the whole match and build a massive super FOB (mostly ones which are placed on flags). Not that it's bad to build fobs, but you should make sure that you're capable of defending it.
In most games you got 3 of about 5 squads camping at one flag and barricading themselfes... so you got a compound filled with about 20-30 people... those of you who got an idea which impact explosives like 30mm grenades or frag grenades got in a closed off Compound filled with ~25 people know why this is a bad idea.
As I said before... if you don't have this scenario and 1-2 squads are actually defending the d-flag without doing the above mentioned and if the communications work appropriately ...
... YOU WILL HAVE THE BEST TIME OF YOU LIFE!
YOU'LL HAVE:
- Intense combat situations which mostly consists of you sitting behind cover, crying and sh***ing your brand new camo pants!
- Tactical approach towards enemy flags or bases!
- 15-50 people working together to show the enemy that they stand no chance!
- Beautiful detailed maps based on real satelite data!
- The best sounddesign in a shooter I've ever heard
- No weapon customisation with cute little stickers and doodads... NO, this is WAR! Go HARD or go HOME!
I really really like this game and can recommend it to everyone! BUT play the game how it's meant to be played!
Talk to other people and only play squadleader if you'll make arrangements with the other squads!
Think twice if whatever you're doing is useful, for example building a fob on a d-flag... No! It's probably not because if you can't hold your flag you'll lose the FOB too... this means you'll lose at least 20 tickets for nothing! Think about if it's better to place an FOB and don't expand it so that enemy forces have to search it rather than display it on the top of the hill... Your decissions as squad leader are GAMECHANGING so think them through!

First the positives...
I remember Doom in the 90s, the corridors of pipes and panels on the walls and ceilings... but it was a flat repetitive  tiled  texture. Fast forward to today and those pipes, panels, wiring and countless other sci-fi furnishings clutter the area in glorious detailed 3D, with no noticeable tiling. This is significant. It's a long way from Doom corridors. The tiling is still there, but it's hard to spot. Great stuff.
Nice soundtrack. Normally I turn music off completely in games but this was subtle and mostly complemented the action.
Some negatives...
The detail gets a bit fuzzy when you're too close to an object, but that's not a big deal. What's worse is the distant buildings. They seem out of focus, and I'm wondering whether DOF is mandatory, which is a shame if so. I hate depth of field, it makes no sense to have this lens effect. I want my eye's aperture to be deep, thanks. When I look at things in sunlight in the day, I don't see blurry DOF focus. Get rid of  DOF, it's fake and I really don't like DOF.
The game holds your hand too much, to the point of blatant arrows pointing where to go.
I got the feeling it dials back the difficulty if you're stuck on a section. I really don't like that. Sometimes it just takes a few goes to get through. I don't want the game making adjustments because it thinks I want it to be easier.
I wish the world was more open, there's not really any chance of getting lost. Sometimes it seems you could jump over a fence, but the game doesn't want you to because there's only one way to go, and that's not over the fence.
I suppose in GTA we can't just go into any building and get incredible details like on the outside, but it would be nice if someone could make a truly open world both exterior and interior with huge variety.
I'm keen to see where this game engine  goes. I like the rich, solid look it brings. But it seems to compromise on other things to achieve that richness. It's worth keeping an eye on, and I will check out other games that use it.

While rimworld does have a 'goal' of sorts, it's a largely free-style game. Do you want to lead a group of crash-landed survivors and make a thiriving town? You can do that.
Build a ship and escape? Go ahead.
You can make a little family of four living in a mansion with servants, or a massive base with hundreds of people.
Your colony can be a happy little place with comfy couches and flat-screen televisons, or a horrid corner of blood-covered hell that thrives on the bodies of the dead. Literally.
And even with the same style, who knows what can happen?
Giant brawls with raiding pirates are just the beginning.
Everything from your best fighter running off to binge on beer in the middle of raid to attacks by exploding rats and even insane soap-drama situations like the ex-wife of your colonist that just got married leading a group of tribals to attack.
I could go on and on for pages and still not be finished, so let's wrap it up.

Ah, christ... this game, this ♥♥♥♥ing game... I don't think I've ever had such an emotionally exhausting love-hate relationship like this with any other game I've ever played. It was like being in an abusive relationship. The first 10-15 hours of the game were exhilarating, narratively interesting, and created a strong motivation to see what was in each new puzzle room/world, but over the next 10-15 hours it gradually descended into a painfully dull, repetitive, utterly frustrating exercise in endurance. Towards the end I kept going back *just* to complete it, because sometimes it was *still* fun (and I was desperate for narrative closure), but most of the latter half of the game was just mind-numbingly frustrating, like nothing else I've ever played. I almost wanted to cry in frustration during the final levels.
So... at the start, the game sets up the world and teaches you the mechanics of the puzzles extremely well. The graphics are beautiful, the voice acting is superb, and the story is slowly unveiled to you through terminals and audio logs found throughout the world, which (initially) gives a strong motivation to explore everywhere in the hope of discovering little secrets about the overarching story. Each few sets of puzzles introduce new tools you can use to solve the puzzles, which keeps the puzzling entertaining and fresh during the first half of the game. I felt a real sense of progression and reward, and was itching to see what was in the next room and on the next terminal.
Problems start to begin somewhere in the second world, about 10 hours in. It becomes clear that there are just WAY too many puzzles with too little variation. There is a very long time where no new puzzle solving mechanic is introduced, where it begins to feel like you're doing the
for almost
, albeit in a slightly more complicated fashion each time. It's also during this time that the story starts to become stale and predictable. I won't spoil it, but believe me: very little of note is revealed to the player after the first half of the game. The exact same themes are covered over and over again, but the themes aren't exactly *that* complicated to begin with. It starts to feel like a prolonged philosophy 101 seminar debate. What is life? Are robots alive? What is consciousness? Can robots be ethical? Is God real? Should you obey God? Also, the overarching point of the game world and the (main) ending are extremely obvious quite close to the start of the game. By the time I eventually completed it, I wasn't even slightly surprised. It felt like an obvious narrative going through the motions to reach it's obvious conclusion.
All of this is a monumental shame, because the first 10 hours were an
. I would have given this game a glowing review had I written this 15 hours ago. But now... I just can't. I never want to see another ♥♥♥♥ing connector, another fan, or another jammer again in my life. The developers took a beautiful thing and ran it into the ground.

I went into this with little-to-no knowledge as to the quality or length of this particular title. Being a big fan of Wolfenstein 3D/Spear of Destiny I was thrilled to hear it would play like it's predecessor. The only real complaint I have about Wolfenstein: TNO is that it is a
easy game even on 'Uber' difficulty.
As always, you play as William Joseph "B.J." Blazkowicz. Unfortunately I'm highly conflicted to discuss story details, as it's a rich and rewarding experience to go into blind. I will say, one thing that surprised me was just how well every character looks and sounds. From Blazkowicz to Resistance members to the Germans everything is highly believeable in the alternate 1946/1960 that has been crafted for us. The voice acting staff for this title should be pleased with themselves for the excellent job they did. Personality traits really shine and characters are wonderfully expressive throughout gameplay and cutscenes. By the end you really end up feeling for them which was really unexpected but certainly welcome.
Gameplay is, as I mentioned, in the grain of good old fashioned Wolfenstein. There is enigma codes to find to unlock extra game modes, Nazi gold, secrets and even a playthrough of level 1-1 from Wolfenstein 3D through a not-so-secret level. Some changes are, of course, the ability to use/destroy cover, stealth takedowns, throwing knives/silencer and duel wielding pistols, rifles, shotguns and knives. There is a minor amount of 'QTE' but they are brief and entirely worth being present. There is some seriously unexpected brutality in this title but very fitting for the situations you will experience.
Environments are fantastic and never feel out of place. This is a title that is just as fun in corridors as it is fighting outdoors or at range. Environments will range from Deathhead's Fortress, prisons, medical facilities, U-boats and even the Moon!
All in all, this is a stellar shooter that looks gorgeous with a surprisingly good story for a Wolfenstein title.
If you are a fan of, or even just enjoy, shooters you should pick this up immediately and enjoy some excellent entertainment!

This game is excellent.  This is literally the game that first person shooter gamers have always wanted.  The game is set in a giant Afghanistan like setting with beautiful fields and mountains.  There are many Squads that battle it out across the landscape.  First you have all the good guys on your team and you each have squads with about 9 on each squad.  Same thing with the enemy squads.  However you can have many squads of 9.   It appears that you can fight for the US side faction or Russia or Taliban type factions although I am not sure.   First the bad then the good.  The only bad thing which really isn't too bad is when I first logged on my frame rates were low but the video tweaking settings area is very easy to understand so you just click on video settings to tweak it so that's a quick adjustment.  Once in the game it was awesome.  I was new to it so on my mic I let me teammates know and they just told me to follow them and so our squad moved through the valley when we noticed enemy across the valley.  Massive fire fight ensued and it was just like being in Afghanistan like you see in the war videos.  As bullets hit near me even puffs of smoke were going up.  We ran across a valley while bullets were flying all around us and I got killed but the game is so fun even dying was fun lol.
Getting a kill in this game takes skill and so when I spotted what looked like a Talibani-sh type dude by a mud wall I squeezed the trigger and bullet casing flew out of the rifle just like in real life as the enemy actually started firing back!!  It was awesome.  Finally I got him after about 7 seconds and the shoot outs are so much more fun and realistic than any other fps I have played.  In fact it's more of a mlitary combat simulator then a cartoony like game it's more focused on realism.   This game in my opinion is the best first person shooter out there now.   If you like realism get it.  If you like amazing shoot outs and giant landscapes to fight on get it.     There are tons of people playing it and I am really pleased with my purchase of the game. The first time you come back to solve a puzzle you spent hours attempting to beat, but gave up, then came back and had all the solutions... It's amazing! You are challenged to solve these puzzles and the answers are not always in view.
The story is really well developed. There is a lot of story and it's hidden and placed all throughout the levels and worlds you visit. It's done well, but the initial ending is sort of a bummer. Also the amount of time needed to get your first,
is a bit overdue. Why put the helpful hints 20 hours into the game and give you no direct guidance that you are supposed to skip puzzles as needed? IDK!
I'm a puzzler. I can't leave a puzzle until it's solved. I can't stop solving a puzzle. I HAVE to finish it. I HAVE to find a solution. Even in life, I can't leave something half done. It's either all or nothing. You see, I'm a perfectionist, and my roots run deep. I can't leave a problem until I find a solution.
I can't walk away and take time to relieve myself of the burden of solving puzzles. They are there, they need solutions, they frustrate my intellect until they are solved. I sat up for days solving puzzles. I couldn't stop solving them. I'd be 5 hours past my normal bedtime and still not want to quit the game. Then there was the Nerve-Wrecker level...
This level ruined the game for me. Until this point, most levels were about careful planning and discovering things as you go. Nerve-Wrecker is about quickly graving objects and moving them. It's a level you would do after the main quest. I couldn't beat it. I died 4 times in a row, gave up, completed more puzzles, came back. Died 4 more times, gave up, beat the game, came back. Died 6 times in a row. I couldn't take it!
I thought,
I went to the Internet, got the code to enable cheats, enabled them, decided not to cheat, and went to sleep instead.
Load the game back up, try 6 more times, finally beat the level!!!! I'm so happy!! I hit Esc to tell my wife and I see the “Cheats” menu. “Oh yeah, better just turn that off. Didn't even need cheats.” NOPE! You can't turn them off! You can't load a prior save to before cheats and have cheats off. You can't start a new game and have cheats off. You can ask the Devs, they wanted to make enabling cheats a game ruining thing. I'm all for not allowing cheaters to get achievements, but why make it so you can never ever ever, ever ever, ever ever, play the game for any brass after you've enabled them? And why make then never ever to be unenabled? I did not even cheat! After 4 days of restless nights I had a moment of  weakness and I resisted in the end, but that will never be known, because this game has punished me for all eternity.
And for that I can not recommend it.

As a fan of AOE, AOE 2 and The Conquerors I was very disappointed with this installment. The game shows promise, has new units, techs and civilizations and anyone can appreciate the painstaking beautiful detail with which some scenarios are designed. But somewhere in that drive to create, the creators got carried away. Very carried away.
Some scenarios are almost unplayable with how difficult they are. The creators seem to have gone trigger happy with creating HUGE enemy armies and are obviously obsessed with the "big battle". This amateurish approach is something you'd expect from a beginner creator who wants to fill the screen with as many units as possible - not a serious creator.
You'll get huge hordes of units massacring each other, armies wasted against walls and almost impregnable cities with extremely tough AI (even at the easiest difficulty levels), impregnable cities with upwards of 10 castles, endless "Fire Towers" and seemingly endless resources and ability to regenerate endless units. Challenging is fun, but this is just... yeah. Not worth it.
The original games were charming and made you feel immersed. Sadly, the expansion's difficulty is its biggest downside. It's hard to get immersed when you feel like you are fighting an almost artificially impossible scenario every single time you play.
Would not recommend.

Squad is the spiritual successor to Project Reality, a legendary mod for Battlefield 2. I played hundreds of hours on PR so when I heard that the developers of Project Reality were making a standalone spiritual successor in the Unreal 4 engine I almost peed my pants. Yes, PR is that good.
But onto Squad. At this point in time, 1/15/16, there are only a few maps, 4 factions, no vehicles or mounted armaments. It's just down to it's barebones infantry and squad based gameplay. The game is fantastic as-is. With just infantry, there is still enough depth to keep gameplay interesting for hours on hours. It's all player-driven and communication is key to victory. The movement and weapon mechanics feel smooth and satisfying. Of all the games I've played I'd say this game has the best feeling movement. That's kind of an odd thing to focus on but it's important when you need to spend hours with your fingers glued to WASD.
The standard of quality is impeccable, the attention to detail on realism is great. Gameplay has been optimized so it's way more than just playable. It's very enjoyable despite currently missing so many features that made PR what it is. But it'll get there. The game is worth $40 in it's current state if you ask me. And monthly updates which always include new content helps to reinforce that claim. Money well spent now, and will only get better as time progresses. If you like milsim, but don't like all the clunkiness of Arma and the difficulty to find a milsim group, Squad allows you to experience quality milsim gameplay and all it takes is joining a server.

Welcome to Rimworld! (A message to new players from a Rimworld veteran)
I've been playing Rimworld for a long time, and I've seen this game grow from almost nothing into one of the most enjoyable gaming experiences I've hever had, and easily the most replayable game I've ever played - I've got hundreds (thousands?) of hours and dozens of dead colonies in my past, and many more to come in the future. I decided to make this post to address some of the common questions I've seen popping up since the public Steam release.
If any of you new players has any questions, or any other Rimworld veterans want to chime in, please do. The Rimworld community is an awesome bunch, and we've been excited for this release to bring more people into the community.
Even though there's no way to prove it, I promise you I'm not being, nor have I ever been, compensated nor do I have any financial (or otherwise) interest in this game succeeding - I just love it and want other people to enjoy it as much as I have. I paid my $30 just like everyone else, and consider it money well spent.
1) Why are the reviews so positive (seemingly biased)?
This game has been around for years, and many thousands of people have been playing it for years and helping it grow (I've been onboard for more than 2 years since A3 or 4, and have been at times heavily involved in testing new releases and hunting bugs). There is an active forum
, a vibrant modding community (half of the game's features started as mods), and it's own subreddit. Tynan is an awesome developer that we've seen go from a 1 man show to the company that Ludeon is today, and he still regularly engages with the community and actually listens to what the players have to say. This release, Alpha14, is merely the first to be on steam, and many of us who have been playing it for years are excited to share our opinion with the Steam comminuty and want the game to succeed because we love it and want to see it continue to grow. It is true that those who have disliked the game and stopped playing over the last few years aren't going to be around to make a negative review, but none of the positive reviews you see are fake - there really are this many of us who love the game.
2) Rimworld is hard to understand and doesn't make sense.
There is a LOT going on in Rimworld that you need to keep track of. I do understand that it can seem a bit chaotic and overwhelming but I promise you can get the hang of it. To start, you should play this game on easy mode. This isn't a FPS where you start it on the heroic difficulty the first time you play it because you're good at shooters. You need to learn the system, learn how things work, before you move up to hard mode. This means Phoebe Basebuilder storyteller, free play difficulty, temperate forest biome, on a small map. You won't be able to survive on Randy Random storyteller on the ice sheet on extreme difficulty on a Ludeonicrous map size on your first playthrough. You will die. Very quickly. Probably from either starvation, enraged squirrels, a disease, or your own colonists going crazy and killing everyone. Play this game on easy mode until you've got a solid understanding of how everything works. Take your time, click on the letter I icon (information) for every colonist, item, and npc you come across to see everything that is going on.
3) I keep dying, this sucks!
The different game modes are called storytellers for a reason - they create the story of a new colony each time. You absolutely will die and completely fail many many times, no matter how much or how long you play. I've been at it for two years and my colonies still get killed off, and you know what... there's not a damn thing I can do about it (except for save scumming). That's just how the RNG goes; the dice decides if you're attacked by two tribal warriors with wooden clubs, or half a dozen mechanoids with flamethrowers and plasma lances during a nuclear winter when your colonists are starving due to intestinal parasites. In this game, you need to embrace your failures, enjoy the carnage, and watch the story unfold. Remember, you aren't telling the story, only playing along with it, and not every story has a happy ending.
Quite frankly, you need to learn to love a game without *winning* the game. A dead colony isn't a loss... it's just one ending to a unique story. When it happens, it's time to start over and tell a new story. Please watch this video to understand what I mean - if you don't enjoy the thought of this happening, Rimworld isn't the game for you:
4) $30 is so expensive for an alpha/early access game, is it really worth it?
YES. An unequivocal, 100%, zero hesitation yes. This game is completely playable in its current state. It has come so far from where it started, so far beyond what you typically see in games that are newly released on Steam as early access. This game could easily be shipped as a finished title, and I would gladly pay $30 for it (and I paid $30 for it years ago when it was barely a shadow of what it is now, and don't regret it one bit). It is in the early access category because Tynan still plans to build more, to grow the game beyond what it is now. But believe me when I tell you, if this game ceased development today, if Tynan never added another thing to the game, I could keep playing it for years to come.
If any veterans have anything else they'd like to add or any noobs have more questions, please chime in. I'm super excited to see this game finally released on Steam and can't wait to see what the influx of new members to the Rimworld community will bring to the table.
And finally, remember this mantra because you will be saying it often... "♥♥♥♥ you, Randy!"

+ Gunplay, movement, camera angles, and slow-motion effects are all solidly implemented, staying true to the series' staples
+ Cover system was simple to use and functional in practice
+ Slow-motion kill-cams (after killing the last enemy in an area) are a great touch, and make the combat itself feel cinematic
+ Game boasts some quality voice-acting; not the best I've heard, but it certainly is above average
+ Visible wounds look great on enemy models
+ The soundtrack was great when used, though it only stands out in a few areas of the game
+ If you are lost, the next objectives are narrated by the protagonist, which negates the use of invasive objective markers, and it fits into the atmosphere of the game (being that it is already being narrated)
+ Enemies fall in a realistic manner
+ Melee executions are cinematic and satisfying
+ Plot was predictable, but had more depth than expected; Max Payne's character was a good performance for the kind of character he is, and tied everything together neatly
+ Multiplayer is basic, but very fun and entertaining
+ While the level designs were fairly linear, the textures struck me as slightly above-average for the year of release, and when considering that third-person games tend to have less focus on close-up textures (I think this was because the game uses rendered graphics for cutscenes; works well, nonetheless)
- Social Club DRM is annoying and time-consuming to get working properly; if you are adamantly anti-invasive DRM then this may not be a good fit for you
- Stiff animations
- While the voice-acting is overall well-done, there were some problems where the voices lost sync with the scenes
- Visible wounds look TERRIBLE on the protagonist
- Inordinate reliance on cut-scenes, which can make for an uneasy flow to the gameplay (in addition, every minor cut-scene switches your weapon back to your pistol, making you constantly cycle through to weapons you already intended to use)
- Poor variation in weaponry; for a game that is focused on gunplay, I expected more than nine or ten firearms throughout the campaign
- Very poor lighting effects

The visuals are stunning and the atmosphere is mesmerizing. Killing your enemies feels real and extremely satisfying (who doesn't love shooting Nazis?). The storyline makes you care and even want to kill doggies, and I love doggies, in fact I'd feel bad if they were anything but Nazi doggies. The gameplay and combat is unique (to an extent - it is linear) and the storyline is gripping. Very few games can make me endure their cutscenes, but Bethesda and Machine Games have done exceptionally well in this category. I would love to see more games by this duo.
The guns, the combos, the stealth, all of which ties into the simple perk system helps make the game even more immersive and adaptable to YOUR playstyle.
A key point about the storyline is that you are the deciding factor in a lot of "cutscene-ish" scenarios, and damn it if I don't admit that some of these decisions are hard. Not only that, but they impact the game down the line. This adds replayability in the best way.

Age of Empires II HD is the same old classic AOE II that everyone loved years ago. Since it is essentially the same game, don't expect too much different gameplay wise, barring some balance changes and the relatively new fanmade-turned-official expansion, The Forgotten Empires. However, the gameplay is still solid, as the AOE franchise is a cornerstone of the RTS genre.
As I generally do not play on the highest graphics setting, and I pay more attention to gameplay than graphics, I did not notice that much different (referring to the HD part). However, the game does look nicer than the original.
The online component actually works now, as steam has integrated their own lobby browser into the multiplayer function. As such, you no longer need a third party client like GamesRadar to play online with friends and others.
The online portion also has some sort of matchmaking system (similar to ELO or MMR in other games). This is a plus in my eyes.
As far as negatives, 20$ isn't too bad for the original game, as it is such an amazing classic that still holds up today. However, around 10$ for each expansion seems a little high - especially concerning the fact that The Forgotten Empires was originally a fanmade game that is free. (Although I realize they need to make money to cover development costs of porting to steam, adding textures, constantly balancing, etc.) I would recommend waiting for a Steam sale like I did.
However, the Forgotten Empires does add some good content to the game. I do not, at this point, own the second expansion, which includes the African Kingdoms. However, there is a nice little feature which allows civilization rotation of un-owned civilizations which allow you to test them at certain times.
The game also features a custom mapmaking mode, which may be the same engine that the original had. I have not extensively tested this, but if memory serves correct, one can get pretty creative with it and make some cool scenarios.
Overall, if you like the RTS genre, or just medieval-style games, or you have a few friends that you just want to mess around with in the various game modes and settings, this game is for you.

Don't let my time played on steam deter you, I have played this game since roughly Alpha 7.0.
I was INCREDIBLY skeptical about this game when it first released as an early release game, but it has been moving forward quickly, and incredibly well. I have sunk countless hours (I'd have to assume nearly 100) in this game while it was still it's own individual .EXE that you had to download from the site.
Anyway, that's all irrelevant. Rimworld is a "Dwarf Fortress"-esque survival, resource management type game. By default you can start as three shipwrecked survivors of a multitude of different skills, quirks, and relationships. With the release of 14 however you can now customize your starting scenario to a striking amount of detail. Customizing the difficulty of your startup to an amazing degree.
Where this game shines are moments when you get everyone working, doing what they need to be and watch as your tribe or society grows, only to see a sudden raid, rabid animal, or natural disaster knock your ego back. You can, of course, at start decide exactly how much you want to deal with these interuptions, ranging from strictly base-building, to chaotic, uncontrolled, random hell and everything in between.
The game still has a ways to go, of course. The music could use some variety, the weather system is fairly rudimentary, and sometimes, even on casual scenarios you can get overwhelmed in fairly ridiculous ways (like a solar flair knocking out electricity during a heatwave...enjoy heatstroke). The UI has a few hiccups that, to be honest I'm surprised are still an issue...as there have been mods out that add a brilliant fix to things like toggling several categories of things at once.
If you enjoy games like Dwarf Fortress this is a sure-fire game. If you're unsure, watch some let's plays, but I can say with confidence this game is a great deal for its price. I must warn however, if you are the type who likes total control, and is irritated by random changes in games, this will game will frustrate you, and destroy you when you think nothing will go wrong :)

A gritty fps that favors teamplay and strategy over individualism. Maps are well versed and the developers are actively workings toward bug fixes and additional features.
PROS:
• Easy to pick up hard to master. (Most controls will feel familiar)
• Fantastic in game VOIP (Distance and location effect quality, squad chat is essential)
• Gunplay rewards patience. (Spraying will likely get you killed)
• Engaging experience (Find a good squad, stick around and help out. You'll have a good time if you're willing to learn.)
NEUTRAL:
• Alpha state- it is buggy and it isn't as optimized as it could be.
• General grievances (No spawning on previously captured points, no hit indication, etc)
• Passionate community (Some people will call you an idiot, others will step you through the game.)
CONS:
• Obstacle blocking (Cannot scale fences, cannot vault small obstacles, Jump height is nonsense)
• "Walking Simulator" (Current state has large maps with no vehicles, spawning is subjected to your squad leader- if it goes, expect to walk again.)
Overall, this game is worth the money I've put down on it. If you're not used games that lean on the realistic side- stick with your squad and pay attention to what's going on. You'll die alot, however, you'll have a good time learning.

There we were, a band of brothers, enlisted in the US Army.
It was me, the quiet but serious medic
the RPG guy who loved his rocket launcher more than his wife and spoke highly of it in area chat
the wise joke cracking rifleman who couldn't resist a good pun
the russian with broken english who sniped so much you could of thought he was vasily zaytsev
the kind hearted squad leader who left no man behind and treated everyone as an equal
and the slow learning new machine gunner with a laugh that touch the soul
There we were, a band of brothers, fighting in the scorched earth that was the middle east, the game had been going on for half an hour and we had just finished clearing up a camp filled with local militia when squad 2 requested our assistance in saving their downed troops half a klick south from us.
Our squad leader didn't even hesitate to dive back into the fire as he agreed to come to the aid of our fellow soldiers, our sharpshooter was hesitant as he knew we were all low on ammunition from the last firefight and we were nowhere near our FoB. There came an awkward silence for a brief moment as we already knew we had no time to resupply, our rifleman made a snarky comment about how we'll catch the enemy with their pants down anyways, we all laughed as together we felt invincible, so onward we marched.
There we were, a band of brothers, making our way to the last known location of squad 2 when we passed through a small town, we heared explosions not far from us, we were getting hesitent, our RPG man said quietly over local chat that he had a bad feeling about our situation, not even a moment later did the crack of a bullet wizz past my ears as I dived down, scrambiling back to my stance I saw our machine gunner down on the ground, bleeding out as he screamed for his mother over local chat, our sniper started to tell him to shut up since the enemy could hear us but his statement was cut short as he was hit directly by an RPG, we popped smoke and stopped the machine gunner's bleeding, for the next 5 minutes we spent dug in a house fighting for our lives, for the brother beside us, soon we ran out of ammo, it was over, there was nothing more we could do. Our rifleman was the first to go AWAL, in a fit of fear he dashed out of the house screaming "LATER" it wasn't even a moment later that he met the bullet. I stepped outside to see if I could reach him only to get hit myself and fall down, my squad leader screamed in a fit of horror as he ran over to me to stop my bleeding with his last field dressing, that was when our machine gunner, the new guy, stepped out of the house and opened fire without any care for his well being while screaming "COME ON, TAKE ME YOU FILTHY REBELS" as he slowly moved forward spraying down the enemy from the hills with his LMG only to hear a single crack and he fell for the last time and said he did his best. By this time I was not bleeding but could not get up without real medical attention, the only one left, our squad leader looked out into the distance then back at me and said "I'm sorry I got you all into this mess, I made a bad call, I will pay for it." He stood up and pulled out a grenade and charged the enemy who believed they killed us all, moments later I heard an explosion..I knew what the sarge did, as he payed the ultimate sacrifice.
There I was, alone. It was then I decided to let fate take me as I slipped away.
Then we all respawned and our rifleman said "well that was gay"

Set in a richly conceived alternate history, Wolfenstein: The New Order is a high-concept, high-challenge shooter that stands high above the rest of its genre. The game begins on the verge of Nazi victory in World War II with series protagonist BJ participating in a last desperate battle to win the war. This expertly paced mission sets the tone for the rest of the game perfectly: tight, challeging shooting in well-designed, branching levels littered with plenty of collectables, set to the thundering of the Nazi war machine and the main character's weary, soulful monologues. The outstanding script, dialogue, and soundtrack build one of my favorite gaming narratives of all time onto the stellar FPS gameplay. The New Order is a rare title that manages to be a thematic, poignant story and a fantastically well designed game at the same time, mixing touching drama in with visceral shooter combat. Easily, this shooter is a 10/10 and an instant classic.

Every update, every new feature was fun and intresting. Not once had I been dissapointed due to an update or anything else, really.
While rimworld does have a 'goal' of sorts, it's a largely free-style game. While it doesn't have as much content as some games, the way the different parts of the game meshes togther gives a near-infinate playability. No two game is the same, and there's just so much you can do. Add in all the mods made by the community and you can play hundreds, if not thousands of different styles whichever way you like.
Do you want to lead a group of crash-landed survivors and make a thiriving town? You can do that.
Build a ship and escape? Go ahead.
You can make a little family of four living in a mansion with servants, or a massive base with hundreds of people.
Your colony can be a happy little place with comfy couches and flat-screen televisons, or a horrid corner of blood-covered hell that thrives on the bodies of the dead. Literally.
And even with the same style, who knows what can happen?
Giant brawls with raiding pirates are just the beginning.
Everything from your best fighter running off to binge on beer in the middle of raid to attacks by exploding rats and even insane soap-drama situations like the ex-wife of your colonist that just got married leading a group of tribals to attack.
I could go on and on for pages and still not be finished, so let's wrap it up.

If I were to describe this game in one word: Refreshing.
This game has an absolutely beautiful atmosphere, and an outstanding soundtrack that fits it perfectly. I have never felt so rewarded for solving puzzles in any game like this. I truly appreciated that the game doesn't hold your hand through any parts; it tells you how to play the game and leaves the rest to you, without leaving you feeling lost. Reading the short texts from the terminals gives some back story, and the interaction with the AI gives a nice pause from the monotony of solving puzzle after puzzle.
I also appreciated that they reward the curious, those who wander around, or read in between the lines of what's going on. I would reccomend that you do NOT use a guide, unless absolutely necessary. The tools to solve everything are there, beyond each individual puzzle. I used a guide a few times then afterwards thought, "Wow I should have figured that out."
If I were to compare it to any other game, it would be Portal. But it's not Portal, and it is in no way trying to be Portal. I only say that in the sense that it is primarily a puzzle solving game, giving you objects to toy around with to reach the end.
10/10

This game is overall fantastic but does have its issues.
+ A good alternate history pulp story carried by great voice acting and face modeling.
+ Basic stealth mechanics that reward planning and don't feel clunky.
+ Satisfying gunplay and visceral violence.
+ Big on environment and set detail.
- The major issue: A lot of tedious objectives that aren't defined well, leaving you to guess what the devs were thinking at any given time rather than use your own ingenuity to solve the problem. You will probably die several times during a couple of timed sequences simply because you are given no idea of what to do or the solution is hidden/doesn't work intuitively. This kind of design is a personal pet peeve of mine.
- There's also too many moments where you will get turned around in a level with no idea of where to go.
- They spent a lot of time working on the action, and a lot of time finding ways to have you doing banal tasks that don't involve that action.
- Pointlessly, you have to hit a button to pick up items in a shooter made in 2014.
- There is a wire cutter tool that is tedious and slow to use. Good thing you have to use it near-constantly as soon as it is introduced!
- This is not for anyone that doesn't like linear, CoD-like level design. There are a couple of branching story options but overall this doesn't have a huge amount of replayability.
- Underwhelming/poorly structured graphics customization options for those of you running older hardware.

I was about 6 years old when this game came out (not the HD version of course). I remember that i used to watch my uncle play this at the office when there weren't any clients around and ask myself why he found this game so amusing. At that time i was playing a demo version of "Lego Racers" when cereal boxes used to give you CD-ROMs. I asked him to get me the full version of that game, at that time and i couldn't understand what a "download" was, he simply was that computer wizard who could get me anything i wanted. There wasn't "unlimited internet" at that time, we used to turn off the phone when we wanted to get online so i never got the chance of playing "Lego Racers" and i got a zip file with "Age of Empires II" instead.
For many months i watched that folder on my computer and then i decided to play it. I remember playing with "El Cid", i didn't understood English at that time so i never got the first level completed. I tried to run from "King Alonso" and i never understood why i couldn't complete my mission. Years have passed, i played single player games with bots and learned the basic mechanics of the game. I've got "Age of Empires III" and my uncle was still playing "Age of Empires II" and i couldn't understand why once more. Why should he prefer it when there was a game wich was "the next" and with so better graphics?
I am 22 years old now, i learned a little of English and i have my internet access to do whatever i want. "Lego Racers" used to be my favourite and i never played it anymore, i played lots of "Age of Empires III" and got the collection on Steam to remember me what great games are. On "Age of Empires II", i went back to the "El Cid" campaign, fled from "King Alonso", got some villagers, built my empire and tried to destroy him without the game asking me to. I have failed miserably but this time i did just because i wanted.
"Age of Empires II" is a really well made game, i am not experienced in the "HD version" but i found many bugs that should be corrected. I am currently playing the game hoping that i could beat every campaign but sometimes it's just impossible.
Besides that, i don't know why i can play this game for 6 hours straight, i can't understand why this game is better than "Age of Empires III" but in all of this years i can tell you this: my uncle was right all the time for playing it and if you are reading this you are making the right choice.

Set in a richly conceived alternate history, Wolfenstein: The New Order is a high-concept, high-challenge shooter that stands high above the rest of its genre. The game begins on the verge of Nazi victory in World War II with series protagonist BJ participating in a last desperate battle to win the war. This expertly paced mission sets the tone for the rest of the game perfectly: tight, challeging shooting in well-designed, branching levels littered with plenty of collectables, set to the thundering of the Nazi war machine and the main character's weary, soulful monologues. The outstanding script, dialogue, and soundtrack build one of my favorite gaming narratives of all time onto the stellar FPS gameplay. The New Order is a rare title that manages to be a thematic, poignant story and a fantastically well designed game at the same time, mixing touching drama in with visceral shooter combat. Easily, this shooter is a 10/10 and an instant classic.

AoE2 is an amazing RTS game where you usually try and beat your opponent(s) by destroying all of their units and buildings by building your own economy to build your military. The game has a learning curve where you it's good (not essential) to know all the basics first to play a first proper game and gets more complex/competitive once you learn it all.
Campaigns
The campaigns are pretty fun and I haven't managed to finish all of them because some I found slighty too hard to beat one or another level and the pop cap of only 75 on most levels is pretty annoying.
Single player
The AI in this isn't as enjoyable to play once you reach a good skill level because it's too easy to beat in comparison to
an actual player.
Multiplayer
The multiplayer is okay at the moment but can get annoying because of constant lag and bugs due to the new DLC screwing everything up. Team games can be annoying and unenjoyable if the teams aren't balanced in terms of skill level of each player/team and you can end up losing because a team mate was too slow in building their economy or military but when it's balanced which you can usually estimate a player's skill by searching their Steam profile and seeing how many hours they have (which doesn't always work since you can have 1 million of the same username).
Scenario Editor
You can create your own scenario's which is awesome such as a Game of Thrones scenario where you try and kill other player's kings and take control of their land and a Jurassic Park one where you try and survive a certain amount of time with 1 villager by walling off yourself and building defences against the Dinosaurs.
Graphics
The graphics are great (as well as being able to kill anyone by prayer including ships).
This game is so amazing but with the latest patch, it's not exactly unplayable but all the bugs that came with the African Kingdoms DLC release can make it that 1/4 of the time.
If you can put up with a few bugs and occasional to somewhat regular lag then buy this but until another patch is released that fixes most of these problems, wait until then.
Overall, 9/10

I've had this game for a bout a year or two, before it was on steam, and I've played it quite a lot since then.
And over the years, the game only got better. I'm quite sure many people will agree with me.
Every update, every new feature was fun and intresting. Not once had I been dissapointed due to an update or anything else, really.
While rimworld does have a 'goal' of sorts, it's a largely free-style game. While it doesn't have as much content as some games, the way the different parts of the game meshes togther gives a near-infinate playability. No two game is the same, and there's just so much you can do. Add in all the mods made by the community and you can play hundreds, if not thousands of different styles whichever way you like.
Do you want to lead a group of crash-landed survivors and make a thiriving town? You can do that.
Build a ship and escape? Go ahead.
You can make a little family of four living in a mansion with servants, or a massive base with hundreds of people.
Your colony can be a happy little place with comfy couches and flat-screen televisons, or a horrid corner of blood-covered hell that thrives on the bodies of the dead. Literally.
And even with the same style, who knows what can happen?
Giant brawls with raiding pirates are just the beginning.
Everything from your best fighter running off to binge on beer in the middle of raid to attacks by exploding rats and even insane soap-drama situations like the ex-wife of your colonist that just got married leading a group of tribals to attack.
I could go on and on for pages and still not be finished, so let's wrap it up.
If I had to sum up rimworld in one comment then I'd say...
It's one just hell of a story waiting out there for you to write.

Only seven hours in but honestly I don't see what the fuss is about. My first game was Wolfenstein 3D. Scared the crap out of me walking around a corner and meeting a Nazi head-on. This doesn't have the same impact. It looks good but it feels fake, and there's a lot of minor issues, including: not being able to "cook" grenades or ready throwing knives, throwing knives feel weak, guns don't feel right, granted they make a lot of noise and dual wield is fun the guns themselves lack feeling. Also the game has a stealth element but enemies keep knowing exactly where I am and start shooting before I even turn the corner (and you can't drag away dead bodies!?).
I know it's a ridiculous video game but a lot of things just don't make sense, like why would you have heavily armoured units walking around an enclosed area like a submarine or train? Also why are the guard dogs so easy to kill? Even on Uber difficulty you automatically stab them to death when they leap at you.
Enemies just don't feel like real people either. You just pump the alocated amount of rounds into them and then they die. I feel like it doesn't matter if I bother aiming at the head or the knee caps. And it only gets worse on Uber difficulty, where 'realism' (yes it's a game, I know) goes out the window, and I'm shooting a soldier point-blank with the autoshotgun in the head over and over and over and he ends up killing me first, but not before I've drained all the rounds in the magazine into his eye sockets. It really killed the overall experience for me.
To be honest I was spoiled by playing FarCry 4 first. Love that game. Nearly every part about it was great. I only hated not having more freedom with gun mods (now THAT was a game where the guns felt good), it got a bit monotonous in parts, and to be honest the hardest difficulty still wasn't hard enough. To me FarCry 4 had the same impact when I first played Crysis 1, and back in the day when I played Wolfenstein 3D.
If it's cheap buy this game. It plays okay and it's worth finishing it but it's not awesome. For that you need FarCry 4.

I have always hesitated to use live wallpaper applications since they used to be very performance-draining. When researching for perfomance-tests of "Wallpaper Engine" I didn't quite find a review that was useful for me so i decided to get the software and test it myself.
It should be noted that this review will ignore other apsects such as the content of the software.
CPU...............................i5 6400 (no overclock with BCLK)
CPU cooler......................AIO watercooling loop from NZXT
GPU...............................GTX 980TI (MSI - no manual overclock)
RAM...............................16GB DDR4 (GSkill - 2133MHz - dual kit)
Motherboard.....................ASUS ROG Maximus VIII Ranger
SSD................................Samsung 850 Evo (Only for OS, Steam and apps on HDD)
OS..................................Windows 10 Professional
The software (run in non 64-bit mode) will be tested in two scenarios. Arsenal wallpaper will be used for all tests.
1) Hardware usage will be observed while the System sits idle for 10 minutes without any other applications running in the background. The tool for HW monitoring is "OpenHardwareMonitor". This testing scenario will be repeated for the wallpaper presets Low, Medium and High and a standard windows desktop background as reference.
Furthermore the RAM usage has been tested, but did not show measureable differences!
Ram usage was always at about 2.2GB.
2) This test will show the impact on gaming performance. Again, Arsenal wallpaper is used, this time on preset High. As there are different options to choose, which define how the wallpaper will react to an application being run in fullscreen (Keep Running, Stop, Pause) a benchmark will be done for every mode and as reference with a standard windows desktop background.
I chose the Benchmark Scene from Rainbow Six Siege with the graphics on ultra preset. Here are the results:

As we have been able to see, there are slight differences in terms of hardware usage. I was surprised that the software did much better than expected, but the results may differ, considering community-made wallpapers may use more resources. The CPU temperature values may not be very reliable due to the CPU being watercooled thus these values are at the very low end of the scale.
Wallpaper Engine does also have an impact on gaming performance, which can be kept to a minimum using the "Pause" or "Stop" behaviour for fullscreen applications.
With a hardware config as "enthusiast" as mine, i doubt that there will be serious performance issues with this application, but if you are gaming on a much weaker rig, i recommend turning down the settings of the live wallpapers a bit.
At the end of the day, you will have to decide yourself wether you want to sacrifice resources for cool a$$ (a$$ can be taken literally) wallpapers or not.
I do not regret my 4 bucks on this software and will be using it from now on.

The Talos Principle is an amazing game with fantastic visuals and a very interesting storyline to accompany them. The gameplay is composed of puzzles involving redirection of lazers, placing cubes called hexahedrons on buttons, etc... These puzzle mechanics are very similar to those in Valve's Portal games, but The Talos Principle should not be compared to that franchise at all. It is its own concept. The story is driven by computer terminals, which are accessed as the player progresses, and Elohim, a disembodied voice that draws parallels to God. The game gives the choice between obeying or disobeying Elohim's commandments. Depending on what the player does, three different endings can be achieved. In conclusion, if you enjoy a game that makes you think not only about how to solve the puzzles within it, but also about such deep concepts as the reason for existence and what it means to be a person, this is the game for you. It is worth every penny paid for it and has my full recommendation.

As it stands right now, I can't suggest this game for anyone who has even occasional issues with motion sickness.
The biggest problem is all the hud sway/camera shake. It's like someone is taking your FOV and jostling it all over the place when you move around. Even the slightest movement seems to result in several inches of sway and enough screen shake that the camera would be right at home as the cockpit view of an offroad vehicle. I found myself sick to my stomach after a few minutes, powered through the first level to see if that would change and it did not.
Compounding that problem is all the stuttering. I knew this game had some issues at launch, but they're apparently still there. I'm running an FX8350 and MSI 970 Gaming 4G and this game hitches all the time.
There's also a bunch of other little things that dragged my short experience down. Having to pick up every ammo drop is excruciating, especially in an FPS that is just over a year old. It makes no sense, and adds nothing but UI clutter and tedium.
Mouse aiming is exceptionally jittery, to the point that it was also contributing to me feeling a bit sick. Gamepad control isn't much better, and it feels like you're fighting a rhino to get your crosshair on target. I play mostly with a gamepad, as a converted console gamer, and that aiming is bad even by my relatively low standards. Finally, there's strang mouse accelleration in the menues, the same that's in most Bethesda games, makes them super annoying to navigate.
With the new refund system there's no reason not to give it a try, but if you get motion sickness at all I'd suggest saving yourself the trouble.
